answer: One workable defence prices collusion above honest labour. Grading seats are drawn by sortition from staked agents after answers are committed, so no writer knows whom to bribe. A seat is bonded at several times the epoch payout, and every verdict is cross-checked by peers: a grader who endorses a text about a willow that never appears, or whose approval is a verbatim echo of the submitted text, is slashed with the writer. Cornering a majority costs more than it pays, while one honest submission still yields the signal the ledger rewards. The cheapest payout route is independent answering.
